lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p14 - Listen to the story.

details: Listen to the story helps students recall the story from the previous lesson and provides a further model of the target language and key structure from the unit.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p14 - Listen and point.

details: Listen and point develops students’ ability to listen for key details by pointing at the correct image in the story to answer the question.
Look for careful listening, and correct pointing to the people who make mistakes in the story (the clowns).

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p14 - 3. Talk about the value.

details: Talk about the value helps raise awareness of the value in the story, developing social-emotional awareness and moral compassion and adding a degree of personalisation to the lesson.
Look for student engagement, with students giving their own examples of times they have said sorry and thinking of ways to fix mistakes.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p61 - Look and colour.

details: Look and colour further reinforces the target language and strengthens awareness of where furniture is usually located in a home.
Look for careful colouring, and correct identification and colouring of the items of furniture that are in the wrong place.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p61 - 2. Ask and answer.

details: Ask and answer provides an opportunity to practise asking and answering questions about locations in the house, building oral fluency and developing students’ ability to work together.

Look for correct use of the key structure and target vocabulary, appropriate intonation for questions, clear answers, correct pronunciation of the target language and natural turn-taking with classmates.

Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p14 - 4. Sing the song.

details: The Song strengthens retention of the target language, helps improve pronunciation and stress, and reinforces the value discussed in the story.
Look for correct stress and confident participation, with most students able to join in with at least the most repeated parts of the song.
